_comment: Authoritative stage map for the Braillewright coding-standards sweep. Read by .github/workflows/phpcbf.yml AND by ops/phpcs_stage_planner.py, so the runner and the planner cannot drift apart. Stage 1 must contain ONLY sniffs whose fix changes whitespace between tokens and never a PHP token; that claim is enforced by .github/scripts/assert-token-stream-unchanged.php.
_token_contract: Every auto-fixable stage MUST declare token_contract, and the workflow picks its gate from that field rather than from anyone remembering which stage is which. 'unchanged' = not one PHP token may differ, proven by assert-token-stream-unchanged.php. 'classified' = tokens are EXPECTED to change, and every change must fall into one of the named token_classes, proven by assert-token-changes-expected.php. Running the 'unchanged' gate against a stage that legitimately changes tokens produces a wall of failures on a CORRECT run, which is the shape this project's CLAUDE.md warns about: a check that cries wolf gets ignored on the run where it is right. Both gates fail closed - an unlisted class is never assumed benign.

_retired.Universal.Operators.StrictComparisons: retired 2026-08-27 - its autofix ships behaviour changes
_retired.WordPress.PHP.YodaConditions: retired 2026-08-27 - pure house style, no fixer exists

1.name: whitespace + layout (autofix, NO token changes)
1._added_2026_08_28: LanguageConstructSpacing and SemicolonSpacing were added on 2026-08-28 because STAGE 2 CREATED THEM. Its include-paren fixer rewrites require_once( X ); as 'require_once  X ;' - two spaces after the keyword, one before the semicolon - so 27 + 27 = 54 brand-new whitespace findings appeared in files Stage 1 had already cleaned. ops/phpcs_stage_planner.py refused to guess where they belonged and exited non-zero naming both, which is the fail-closed path working. Both were confirmed auto-fixable from the CI log's [x] markers (54 of them, matching exactly) before being placed here, and placing them in Stage 1 asserts they change no PHP token - a claim assert-token-stream-unchanged.php then has to prove on the next dispatch rather than anyone taking it on trust. GENERAL LESSON: a token-changing stage hands work back to the whitespace stage, so run Stage 1 again after Stage 2 - and expect the same after Stage 4.

2.name: syntax normalisation (autofix, tokens change, behaviour does not)
2._token_classes_note: Each class is a transformation assert-token-changes-expected.php can recognise structurally and argue is inert; the argument for each one is written next to its rule in that script. The list is an ALLOW-LIST: an edit matching no class fails the gate. Measured on the 2026-08-28 Stage 2 patch (44 files) - if a later WPCS bump adds a sniff to this stage, its edits will land as UNCLASSIFIED and stop the run rather than passing as already-approved.
